description: Sync opportunities, leads, tasks, projects, people, companies and logged activities from one Copper account. Copper permissions are not imported.
opening: Sync a whole Copper account: opportunities, leads, tasks, projects, people, companies, and the notes and logged interactions on them. Each record or activity is one document. An activity links to the record it is logged on.

There is nothing to select. Everything the API key can read syncs. Copper permissions are not imported, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Records deleted in Copper stay in HydraDB. Activities with no text, such as stage changes, are skipped.

connect.auth: Copper uses an API key together with the email of the Copper user the key belongs to.

credentials.name: user_email
credentials.text: The email of the Copper user the API key belongs to.

steps.title: Get an API key
steps.text: In Copper, get an API key. Note the email of the Copper user it belongs to.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the key as `api_key` and the user's email as `user_email`.

steps.title: Configure the connector
steps.text: There are no resources to select. The connector syncs everything the key can read in the account.

connect.account: One connector reads one Copper account.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads records and activities modified since the last sync.
sync.edits: An edited record is read again and updates its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted records are not removed. A record deleted in Copper stays searchable in HydraDB.
notes: If the account does not have a Copper add-on feature enabled, the record type that needs it is skipped with a warning and the other types still sync.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.copper_id
shared_attributes.text: The Copper record id. Targets one record, and keeps later syncs on the same document. Tasks carry a `task:` prefix and projects a `project:` prefix, so include it when you filter on a task or project. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.copper_object
shared_attributes.text: The record type, such as `opportunities`, `people` or `activities_search`. Limits a query to one type. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Opportunities, leads, tasks and projects
documents.one_document: One opportunity, lead, task or project.
documents.title: The record's name.
documents.text: The record's free-text details, then `Label: value` lines. Opportunities: `Name`, `Company`, `Status`, `Value` with its currency, `Close date` and `Assignee`. Leads: `Name`, `Company`, `Title`, `Status`, `Value`, `Email` and `Assignee`. Tasks: `Name`, `Status`, `Priority`, `Due date`, `Tags` and `Assignee`. Projects: `Name`, `Status`, `Company`, `Tags` and `Assignee`. The name is searchable too.
documents.date: When the record was last modified, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: None. Use `additional_metadata.copper_id` to find the record in Copper.

attributes.name: assignee
attributes.text: The assigned user's name, or their email when the name is missing, written as the `Assignee` line. The graph records the record as assigned to that person.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: The Copper status, such as Open, Won, Lost or Completed, written as the `Status` line.

attributes.name: monetary_value
attributes.text: An opportunity's or lead's value, written as the `Value` line.

attributes.name: company_name
attributes.text: The related company's name on opportunities, leads and projects, written as the `Company` line.

attributes.name: close_date
attributes.text: An opportunity's close date, written as the `Close date` line.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: A task's priority, written as the `Priority` line.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.text: A task's due time, written as the `Due date` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the record was created, written as a `Created` line. Used as the result date only when the modification time is missing.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the record was last modified. Not searchable.

attributes.name: pipeline_id
attributes.text: An opportunity's pipeline id. It is not turned into a name.

attributes.name: pipeline_stage_id
attributes.text: An opportunity's stage id. It is not turned into a name.

attributes.name: completed_date
attributes.text: When a task was completed. It is not the result date.

attributes.name: object_type
attributes.text: The record type. Filter on it with `additional_metadata.copper_object`.

documents.name: People and companies
documents.title: The person's or company's name.
documents.text: The record's free-text details, then `Label: value` lines. People: `Name`, `Company`, `Title`, `Emails` and `Assignee`. Companies: `Name`, `Email domain` and `Assignee`. The name is searchable too.
documents.date: When the record was last modified, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: None. Use `additional_metadata.copper_id` to find the record in Copper.

attributes.name: assignee
attributes.text: The owner's name, written as the `Assignee` line, where HydraDB can identify the person. It does not create an assignee relationship.

attributes.name: company_name
attributes.text: A person's company, written as the `Company` line.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: A person's job title, written as the `Title` line.

attributes.name: email_domain
attributes.text: A company's email domain, written as the `Email domain` line, so a company can be found by its domain.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the record was last modified. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the record was created. Used as the result date only when the modification time is missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: object_type
attributes.text: `people` or `companies`. Filter on it with `additional_metadata.copper_object`.

documents.name: Activities
documents.one_document: One note or logged interaction that has text. Activities with no text, such as stage changes, are skipped.
documents.title: `Comment by` and the name of the user who logged it. Without an author, the first 80 characters of the text. The activity type is not used as the title and is not searchable.
documents.text: The activity's details text, with the author, the record it is logged on, and its created and updated times.
documents.date: When the activity record was last modified, else when it was created.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The user who logged the activity, as a name. The graph records the activity as written by that person.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The record the activity is logged on, written as a `Parent` line. Links the activity to that record when it is a person, lead, opportunity, company, project or task.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.copper_parent_id
attributes.text: The bare id of the record the activity is logged on, with no prefix. Returns every activity logged on one record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the activity record was last modified, written as an `Updated` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the activity record was created, written as a `Created` line. Used as the result date only when the modification time is missing.

attributes.name: activity_date
attributes.text: When the activity happened. It is not the result date.

attributes.name: parent_type
attributes.text: The type of record the activity is logged on: person, lead, opportunity, company, project or task.

example_searches: Which opportunities for Acme are open and what are they worth?
What was the last note logged on this lead?
Which tasks are due this week and who owns them?

connections: An activity to the person, lead, opportunity, company, project or task it is logged on.
An opportunity to its company and its primary contact.
A task or project to its related record, and a project to its company.
A link is made only to record types this connector syncs. No links to other tools.
people: The assignee of each opportunity, lead, task and project.
The assignee of a person or company appears only in its text.
graph.from_text: The free-text details of every record, the `Label: value` lines, and the text of notes and logged interactions.

not_synced: Activities with no text, such as stage changes.
Pipelines, stages, tags, lead statuses, loss reasons and other Copper settings, as documents of their own.
Deletions: deleted records stay in HydraDB.
